images.title: A parallel line, tilted
images.purpose: Show the parallel line construction on a steeply slanting line m, by copying the corresponding angle at A to B.
images.composition: Line m slanting steeply on the left, line n parallel to it on the right, the transversal l crossing both; open white space top and bottom.
exact_structure: A long dark line m slanting steeply from lower left to upper right on the left side of the frame, labelled m.
A point B to the right of m, labelled B; a dark line l through B that cuts m at A, labelled A and l, running from left to right across the frame.
At A, a grey (#6B7280) arc cutting m above l and cutting l between A and B, with a short dashed amber (#E69F00) chord between the two cut points (the cut points are not labelled).

At B, a grey (#6B7280) arc of the same radius cutting l on the side of B away from A, with a short dashed amber (#E69F00) chord of the same length from that cut point to a point on the arc above l (not labelled).
A long reddish purple (#CC79A7) line n through B, parallel to m, labelled n.
Matching single arrowhead marks on m and on n, pointing the same way, to show they are parallel.
One small reddish purple (#CC79A7) angle arc at A between l (towards B) and m (above l), and one of the same size at B between l (away from A) and n (above l): corresponding angles.
rejection: the angle arcs at A and B placed in non corresponding positions, or of different sizes
the two amber chords of different lengths, or the arcs at A and B of different radii
images.takeaway: Copying the corresponding angle at any point gives a parallel line, whatever the direction of m.
images.description: A steep line m, a transversal l through B, matching grey arcs and amber chords at A and B, and a reddish purple line n through B parallel to m.
images.context: Shown beside the concept text and video for this concept.
images.teaching_notes: Find the two matching angle arcs first, then follow the arcs and chords that copied one onto the other.

image_decisions.why: A tilted version shows the method does not depend on m being horizontal.
